about: Driftwake's timeline, one entry per version, oldest first. Each release: fill in its entry (status "shipped", date, headline, img, added, news), set "here" to it, and move the next one to "building". An unstable release (an early build, a GitHub pre-release) gets "unstable": true: the timeline leaves it out and "here" stays on the last stable one. Images are names in /img (name.jpg and name-640.jpg; early/ holds the v1.5-era shots); clips are names in /img/clips (name.jpg + name.gif). Use Driftwake's own names (docs/originality_plan.md).

versions.name: Prototype
versions.headline: Where it started: procedural islands, an ocean, a sword and a ship.
versions.alt: A small green island with a lighthouse, ringed by turquoise shallows in open sea
added: Procedural islands, an ocean to sail, sword combat, a ship and loot banking.

versions.name: Brinehollow
versions.headline: The first real build: the island of Brinehollow, a sloop and a PS1 renderer.
versions.alt: Brinehollow's village: timber houses along a dirt lane, the lighthouse on the hill
shots: early/tavern
Inside the tavern: a bar with bottles on the shelves, plank floors and a lamp
early/outfits
Six captains from the character creator in different outfits
added: A village, a tavern, a market, a lighthouse, ruins and the smugglers' camp.
A character creator, procedural anime-style bodies, and hair and cloth physics.
An inventory, gear, and villagers with branching dialogue.
Pirate grunts (swordsmen and riflemen) and scuttlebugs.
Parries, ragdolls and the plunge attack.
The sloop, swimming, and the PSX renderer.

versions.name: Skills and Crew
versions.headline: Skills, fighting styles and co-op for up to four captains.
versions.alt: A crew of captains fighting pirates round a campfire on the beach
shots: coop
Three captains with swords drawn on the deck of their sloop at sunset (current build)
added: A skill bar and energy, and the first Driftfruit powers.
Levels and the skill map, with Iron Will and Weather Eye.
Sword, dual swords, boxing, pistol and dual pistols.
Blocking, red unblockable attacks, fall damage and foot IK.
A title screen and three save slots.
Co-op for up to four captains
Knocked-out crewmates can be revived, and the crew shares one ship.

versions.name: Pirates
versions.headline: Ships at war, Redtide Rock and its captain, and music for every place.
versions.alt: Four pirate ships under black and red sails on the open sea
added: Crew-manned cannons and broadsides, plus pirate ships that hunt, fire and board.
A fort guarded by Captain Morrow, "Red Tide", a three-phase boss.
Generated tracks for the island, the sea, combat and boss fights.
A loot window, drag-and-drop inventory, and trading between captains.

versions.name: Weather
versions.headline: A day and night cycle, storms with lightning, and a sea rebuilt from real wave trains.
versions.alt: The sloop running before the wind across rolling waves toward Brinehollow
added: A 24-minute day/night cycle with a sky, sun, moon and stars.
Clear, cloudy, rain and storms, with lightning and rough seas.
3D puff clouds you can fly through, and god rays.
Waves rebuilt from six wave trains so swimmers and ships ride the waves you see, and the sea fades into the horizon.

versions.name: Steel and Style
versions.headline: The katana, pistols that aim, and bodies that move like bodies.
versions.alt: The captain leaping into a katana air slash on the beach, a purple arc behind the blade
added: A two-handed style with a scabbard, a charged iai draw, a running draw and an air slash.
Shots follow the crosshair, dual pistols get the Gun Rain air attack, and gun kata works on the move.
Skinned bodies with round knees, elbows and shoulders, and fuller body shapes.
Hip and leg motion, uneven landings, skids and planted stops.
They no longer slide or vibrate, and they collide with themselves.

versions.name: The Open Sea
versions.headline: Real sailing, sea hazards, plunder, the first Leviathan and enemy fleets.
versions.alt: A Leviathan's coils breaking the waves beside the sloop
shots: early/whirlpool
A whirlpool spinning in the open sea
early/shipwright
A red-hulled ship at Tackett's pier
early/title
The title screen at sunset with the v1.5 version ribbon
versions.clipAlt: The sloop runs under full sail past dark sea cliffs
added: Wind and sail trim, an anchor on a chain worked at the capstan, and hulls that hole, burn and flood while the crew patches, pumps and douses.
Reefs, fog banks, whirlpools and drifting storm cells.
Wrecks to loot, messages in bottles and buried treasure.
A serpent at its lair with bites, tail slams and a hoard.
Sloops, gunboats, brigs and Admiralty ships that ram, flee and surrender. You can board their ships, and their crews are visible on deck.
A sea chart, a compass strip and map marks.
Brinehollow's traders and Tackett the shipwright
Refits, paint, a flag designer and figureheads.
Seven item tiers, 27 weapon designs, new armour (cuirass, mail, morion, greatcoat, gauntlets, greaves and capes), nine more hairstyles, and hats that sit over the hair.
The axe gets its own moveset, and the cutlass is polished with a running cut.
Foam wakes, turquoise shallows and rain pooling on deck.
Smoother co-op sailing, and levels now take twice the XP.
A What's New pop-up and a version ribbon.

versions.name: Trees and Timbers
versions.headline: Skill trees, an ultimate for every weapon, and bigger ships with a cabin.
versions.alt: The captain swinging an axe technique, a pale blue crescent of force in front
shots: early/whirlwind
The captain spinning an axe whirlwind through pirates on the beach
added: A tree for every weapon, Base & Will and your Driftfruit, grown with weapon mastery. Old saves get every skill point back.
Riposte, Wind Severer, Blade Dance, Deadeye, Smoke Bomb and more, and an ultimate for every weapon, on R.
Suplex, Shoulder Throw, Giant Swing, Hundred Fists, Rising Dragon and the Leviathan Fist.
Squall Step becomes Shadow Step, Foresight a stance that dodges for you, and Ballast hardens you by itself.
A parry upgrade that cuts gunshots out of the air, and sends them back once mastered.
17 new passives, and Captain's Will at level 20.
A quarterdeck over a crew cabin, a crow's nest, rigging and swing ropes.
A bunk, a galley and the crew's shared chest. You wake in the cabin when you fall, and your bag waits on a grave.

versions.name: Wind and Story
versions.headline: A story to start, Brinehollow's forest and harbour town, and fairer sea fights.
versions.alt: The captain, sword drawn, walking up to a mossy cave mouth, glowing fungus inside
added: Wake on the beach past the quay and follow Old Pell's lead through Brinehollow to Captain Morrow, with your next goal on screen and a marker to follow.
A deep western forest, Captain Grell's pirate den, spitters in the canopy and the Brood Queen's cave.
A stone quay with piers, trading ships and a harbour tower. The village gets dressed houses, a furnished tavern, a cobbled plaza, a smithy and a sea chapel.
Hold L to see where the islands of the chain lie.
A new cutlass combo and polished techniques (the Kraken's Wake), elements woken by weapon mastery, and heavy attacks that tire you when spammed.
Enemy hull bars, far fewer holes, faster pumping, and ships that ram or board up close instead of firing. The wind only ever helps.
The fort's guns are gone; a stone stair, sea stacks and crags instead.
Sound and sight of the sea
Surf, swell, hull wash, creaking timbers, gusting wind and whistling rigging; surf rolling in, whitecaps, wind streaks and spray.
And interaction prompts only when you're right next to things.

versions.name: The Chain
versions.headline: Past Redtide, the lodestone leads on to a chain of islands made from your world's seed.
versions.alt: The captain on an overgrown jungle trail, a stepped stone pyramid rising out of the trees
added: Past Redtide, the lodestone leads to islands generated from your world's seed. Jungle isles have a pirate camp and its named captain, a bug lair, ruins and a summit lookout, and each one is tougher than the last.
An inn, a trader and a cook, a job board and an elder on every island.
Each jungle isle's beast, with its hoard and the Silverback Pelt.

Needles on the compass, each island's theme and danger, forks you pick by sailing, and a chart that follows you along the chain. The needle settles after 15 minutes on an island, or as soon as its beast falls.
Pirate fleets at the next island's level, hazards, Leviathans, wrecks, bottles and islets on every leg.
The katana and the axe reworked (Thousand Petals, Maelstrom, Earthsplitter), and jumping attacks for every weapon.
Layered hull wash that follows your speed, footsteps by surface, varied hits and shots, and island music that resumes after a fight.
Slower levelling, weaker long-range pistols, faster and fiercer pirate ships.
Guests see boarders, and late-built islands catch up on fights.
Playable at driftwake.fun (co-op stays on desktop).

versions.name: Beasts and Blades
versions.headline: The Silverback and the Leviathan rebuilt, and the Corsair's sword and pistol.
versions.alt: The Silverback crouched in its jungle clearing
added: The Silverback is a real gorilla now, and the Leviathan is a long serpent that circles your ship, rears over the deck and bites.
The Corsair style puts a blade and a pistol in one combo, with Powder Lunge, Dead Man's Drop, Powder Finale, a butt-strike while you reload, and its own skill tree with an ultimate.
Fixed and polished. Pair a sword with a second sword, an axe or a dagger: the off hand changes the weight of each hit, and Twin Spin is in the tree.
Chests no longer hold them while their powers are reworked. Fruits you've already eaten stay yours.
A pistol shot fired across your own body no longer vanishes, and a guest who reaches an island that's still building keeps its fights.
The starter island is built from reusable pieces, the first step to giving every chain island its level of detail.

versions.name: The Living Isles
versions.headline: The biggest update yet: every island its own adventure, with harbours, villages, caves and jungle bosses.
versions.alt: Net menders on the beach of a stilt harbour at sunset, the sloop at the pier
shots: temple
The captain fighting giant bugs in a ruined temple's pillared hall
shade
The Shade, a huge black panther, pouncing at the captain under the canopy
versions.clipAlt: The captain blinks around a pirate eight times with two daggers, drawing a star of green streaks
added: The brood queen, Captain Grell and Captain Morrow get gap closers with clear tells, poison leaves puddles, the riflemen's shove has a readable wind-up, and pirates have more moves, flank in groups, and the tougher ones dash out of the way.
23 new pieces of clothing and armour, from a kettle helm and a kimono to sabatons, brass goggles and a fur mantle. Sela sells the cloth and leather, Vey the steel, and the crown is plunder only.
A clifftop plateau out of sight of the wake-up beach, reached by a pillar-hopping climb along a knife-edge ledge or a rope ladder from its pier.
Every chain island's pier is a whole harbour district, in one of five kinds: a stilt port, a smugglers' cove, a busy wharf, a crumbling old harbour, or a bare landing.
Towns, hamlets, walled trading posts, stilt villages and old ruins. Every one has an inn, a trader, a cook, an elder and a job board, and you can walk into the shops and homes.
Fifteen to twenty people on each island with daily routines. Three named locals on every island have their own talk, rumours and quests.
Caves, dungeons and the ruined temple
One to three caves on every island from seven kinds, each ending in a boss and a reward. Some islands hide a ruined temple: two levers, a bronze gate and the Warden behind it.
Six kinds of forest, giant canopy trees and thick undergrowth that slows you down off the trails, with the jungle's own music, ambience and weather.

Waterfalls, wrecks, great trees, step pyramids, watchtowers, totem groves, mines and gorge bridges, plus one set piece per island, from a sunken village or a volcano vent to a giant skeleton or an old fort.

The Silverback takes to the canopy and drops on you from above. The Strangler (a giant snake), the Shade (a big cat that stalks you through the brush) and the Mantis Queen share its throne, with an alpha boar and the Thornback as minibosses.
Boars, leaping and rolling bugs, swarming mites, burrowers, bats, toucans, monkeys, snakes and crabs, with fireflies and butterflies on top.
Jagged sea cliffs and sea stacks, and long sandy shelves you can wade out on.

A new weapon in five designs at every tier. One dagger or two: each set has its own combo, Shadow Lunge, a jump attack, a skill tree and an ultimate (Red Eclipse and Hundred Fangs). Crits, bleeding wounds and backstabs.
Weapons in your hands no longer take bag space, and tooltips compare damage, speed and range against what you're using.
Option selectors step both ways, islands load more smoothly, and co-op fixes for ruined villages and crewmates at the helm.

versions.name: Sea Legs
versions.headline: The feel update: how your captain moves, rests, sneaks, heals and shows off.
versions.alt: The captain jogging across a town plaza at dusk while villagers gather round the fire
added: Standing, running and sprinting jumps with their own take-offs and landings, a somersaulting double jump, a snappier dash, and the lodestone (L) held up properly.
Every weapon kind draws and puts away its own way, with 13 new sounds; axes now hang on your back.
Food, rum, stew and the new Sea Tonic share an 8 s cooldown and take a moment to eat or drink; a hit, roll or knockdown spills it.
Benches, stools, logs, crates and Morrow's chair (F), or the ground from the emote wheel; ship seats sail with you.
C crouches: quieter steps, and grunts and creatures notice you at half range, much less from behind.
Hold T for a wheel of twelve, seen by your whole crew.
Captains and villagers gesture as they talk; chests open with both hands, levers are hauled and items are handed over.
Layers sit properly over each other, and nine new pieces, from a slouch hat to cavalier boots and a spyglass.
The skill map, shops, dialogue, the chart, saves, the creator and the HUD all draw at a whole-number scale.
A save made in the first moments after loading could send you back to the dock.

versions.name: Night Watch
versions.headline: Light, music and a living sea: the world after dark, and how it sounds.
versions.alt: A jungle town at night: lit windows and lanterns round a plaza with a fire
added: Moonlit blue nights instead of black ones, plus more lamps, lit windows and doorways across every town and harbour.
Every captain wears a brass lantern at the hip that lights itself at dusk and swings as you run; L toggles it.
Six on your ship, two on pirate ships, so you can spot them from far off at night.
A new title theme, and longer pieces for the open sea, the island wilds and the villages, each with a night version that fades in on the same bar.
A bow wave that grows with speed, spray and mist, surf that breaks differently on beaches, rocks and quays, spindrift and drifting foam.
A deep swell, lapping, far breakers, rock crashes and wind gusts by distance to the real coast, all muffled when you dive.
Gulls round the harbours and following your ship, high flocks over the islands and parrots in the jungle.
Rain that splashes on ground, roofs and decks, puddles that build up and dry out, and rings on the sea.
Daylight lasts 14 minutes and the night 10, in the same 24-minute day.
Pixelation is one on/off option (F2), and the lodestone moved to H.

versions.name: Shore Leave
versions.headline: Instruments, shanties and duels: things to do with your crew when nobody's trying to sink you.
versions.alt: A stilt village at golden hour, villagers on the raised deck
added: A tin whistle, a bodhran, a concertina, a fiddle and a hurdy-gurdy. Wear one in the INST slot and hold T to play.
Four original shanties, each with a part for every instrument. Join a crewmate who's playing and you come in on their tune at the same spot.
Challenge a crewmate (F): only the two of you can land a blow, the loser just gets knocked down, and the winner gets a little XP.
Blades slice, axes chop, fists thud, shots smack, and parries ring steel on steel, for every attack, yours and the enemies'.
Sounds for hover, confirm, back, equip, buy and sell, level up, and quests.
The waves no longer jump after a hitch.

versions.name: Smooth Sailing
versions.headline: The performance update: Brinehollow from about 24 to 108 fps, with the same look.
versions.alt: The captain on a palm beach squaring up to a colony of purple crabs
added: Pirates, bugs, enemy ships and villagers far from every captain stop thinking and animating, and wake up exactly where they were, in co-op too.
Characters drawn in about 15 pieces instead of 23, small props fade out at a distance, and fog banks are drawn as one.
Hitboxes stopped constantly checking for overlaps, moored ships rest until you come near, and a slow frame can't snowball.
Weather, birds, clouds, shore sounds, spray and puddles update a little less often.
Brinehollow on the dev laptop: about 24 to 108 fps at midday, 28 to 107 at night, 31 to 99 in rain. F8 shows enemies awake and asleep.
Lower, wider twin daggers, dual swords lower, each with its own block, parry and flourish.
Arms no longer stretch after knockdowns; combos, reloads and buffered inputs count in game time.

versions.name: Cliffs and Currents
versions.headline: The cliff path to Grell's den, and water that knows where the shore is.
versions.alt: The sloop under sail past a dark wall of sea cliffs topped with jungle
added: A ledge cut into the sea cliff, twice as long, with gaps that drop to the sea, a bug cave with a cave brute, and a broken bridge you cross on a hanging chain.
Grell's pier ladder stays rolled up until someone reaches the top the hard way, then it's a shortcut for the whole crew.
Waves calm over the shallows and roll in along the beach, sheltered coasts are calmer, and the sea never comes up through the sand.
Cannon smoke banks, fireballs on hulls, water plumes and real dust clouds from heavy hits.
Letting go of a vine, a ship's rope or a chain keeps your momentum.
Sprint shake, thunder, villager barks and the weather run on game time, so a hitch can't throw them off.

versions.name: Sand and Snow
versions.headline: The chain goes past the jungle: snow and desert islands, each with its own towns, beasts, weather and music.
versions.alt: The captain walking into a snow village of round pink-brick houses, a castle on the peak behind
shots: desert
A packed desert medina of pastel houses with domes and minarets
sandstorm
The same medina swallowed by an ochre sandstorm
added: A tall peak with frozen lakes and a river, a castle on the summit, pink-brick villages under tiered green roofs, a buried town, a ship frozen into the pack ice, and ice caves.
Wolf packs, white bears, walrus bulls, hares and stampeding shagbacks. Bosses: the White Shade, the Bear King and the Ice Golem, with Frostfang and the Rimeback.
The biggest islands yet: plateaus, mesas, dunes, canyons and oases, pastel towns and packed medinas, caravan camps, a buried city and a tomb in the cliffs.
Scorpions, monitor lizards, fennec foxes and vultures. Bosses: the Sand King (a sandworm that hunts from under the sand), the Dune Emperor, the Basilisk and the Sand Lion.
Snow always falling with the odd blizzard; deserts never rain, but sandstorms roll in.
Boot prints in snow and sand that slowly fill back in, your breath in the cold, and footsteps that sound like the ground on every island.
Desert and snow tracks for the wilds and the towns, each with a night version, plus wind, sandstorm and blizzard ambience.
Smoke, dust, sand, snow, mist and blood from a new sprite library; the cutlass's Kraken's Wake pours out ink-drawn water.
Tattered capes with painted folds, and a heavy cloak from Sela.
Minibosses turn up on every kind of island.

versions.name: Timber and Tide
versions.headline: Forest islands, a sloop you build up, and Brinehollow grown into a real town.
versions.alt: A lumber town of log cabins among autumn woods of red, orange and gold
shots: sloop
A fully upgraded sloop at Brinehollow's harbour: plated hull, extra guns, lanterns and a tangerine grove
brinehollow
Brinehollow from its harbour: a market street climbing to a shrine terrace and pagoda
added: Autumn woodland with rivers that fall into gorges, a lumber town with a water-wheel sawmill and a log flume, a ruined castle and a hollow giant tree.
Red deer, foxes, will-o'-wisps, wood sprites and walking stumps. Bosses: the Stag King and the Elder Treant, with the moss golem, the Cursed Huntsman and his hounds, and the Wild Hunt at night.
Tackett's refits are twelve upgrade lines with levels, each one visible on the sloop, paid with gold and salvage. In co-op anyone can chip in.
A SEA skill tree for each captain, earned by sailing, gunnery, repairs and the pump.
Farmland, a windmill hamlet, a waterfall pool, a wreck and a second cove; a market street, a second row of houses and a shrine terrace with a pagoda.
Shopkeepers on daily routines, the Salted Gull busy at night, lanterns across the market street, and a busier harbour.
Every building has a proper door and steps you can walk up.
The combo, the air slash and all five skills follow the blade's real path, with drawn steel slashes and a sakura awakening.
Co-op guests' clocks settle right after joining.

versions.name: Charted Waters
versions.headline: Everything you do makes you better at it: skills, food, fishing, diving, a map in your hands and a journal for the crew.
versions.alt: The captain fishing off a pier at golden hour, the line out to a bobber on the waves
shots: dive
The captain diving over a reef beside a sunken chest
heldmap
The captain holding a parchment map, fog over the unexplored parts of the island
versions.clipAlt: The captain casts, the bobber dips, and a fish comes up on the line
added: Fewer, bigger nodes; a shared Captain tree on level points, weapon trees that grow as you fight, and weapon families that share mastery.
Swimming, Seamanship, Cooking and Fishing level up by doing them, with perks at milestones.
Much scarcer drops, rolled for each captain; from blue rarity up, every weapon has a named trait that changes a move.
Each shop is a trade with a stock that changes every day, buy-back, rare gear only at treasure merchants, and artisans camped on the islands' trails.
Heal in a fight from the quick item; cook ingredients at the galley or a campfire into meals with 10-20 minute buffs.
Four rods, four baits, a cast-wait-strike minigame on the real waves, and 21 catches from common to legendary.
Dive for chests, oysters and reefs with a breath meter; currents, surf and cold water; sharks, morays and jellyfish; new strokes.
A parchment map in your hands, fog over what the crew hasn't explored, ? marks, and a zoom out to the sea chart.
Multi-step quests from people, notice boards and things you find, handed back to whoever gave them; villagers' own lines and ten kinds of encounters.
Lash the helm, then train, read, tinker, fish or sleep while she holds her heading.
Abilities on 1-5, weapon loadouts, an action wheel, making camp, an equipment slot, crew chat and shift+click.
Swinging ropes as a yard upgrade, and enemy crews that board you.
Smoother towns and island loads, steadier co-op joins, and many smaller fixes.

versions.name: A First Look at the Capital
versions.headline: A sneak peek at the first real city: a walled royal capital two islands out from Brinehollow.
versions.alt: A walled white city on the sea at sunset, a lighthouse on the harbour mole and a palace on the hill behind
shots: capital-plaza
The capital's plaza by day: a fountain, market stalls and banners, the palace on its hill
capital-night
The plaza at night, lit windows on every floor
added: The chain's first city stop: a walled capital with a harbour, a lighthouse and fort, towers, and a palace on a hill. Its name is rolled per world.
The market plaza and shops, the Crown and Compass inn, a notice board and city quests, the palace gate and the arena's walls, and Gallows Row's toughs.
The busiest streets in the game, the same on every crewmate's screen.

versions.name: Every Wake a Lesson
versions.headline: Skills rebuilt: weapon trees that grow as you fight, captain talents and Will, adventure trees, one skill bar for every weapon, and a new hand-made look.
versions.alt: The skills menu: a katana's tree of glowing nodes in three branches on a night sky, under wooden sign tabs
shots: skill-trees-captain
The Captain tab: a level trunk with talent choices and the Will path beside it
radial-wheel
The action wheel, round with icons, over Brinehollow's square
added: Nine weapons, each with its own tree in three branches that grows only while you fight with it: moves and techniques by mastery level, stat steps for points, versions you switch at the ship's bunk.
Tougher every level, milestones and a talent every five levels; Will from beating great foes.
Sailing, swimming, cooking, fishing, acrobatics, defense, stealth and tinkering, each appearing the first time you earn it.
Any weapon's skills from your loadouts on 1-5 and R (using one switches to that weapon), three passive slots and a library.
Menus, dialogue, signs and round wheels in a hand-made seafaring style.
Islands built off the main thread, no freezes when islands are let go or fights start, occlusion in towns.

versions.name: New Ways to Fight
versions.headline: Five new weapon kinds, a stance for every weapon, and controller support.
versions.alt: The skills menu: a weapon's tree of glowing nodes in three branches on a night sky
added: Polearms, hammers and kanabo, twin axes, greatswords and Black Leg kicks, each with a stance, moves, a tree, an element and an ultimate.
Every weapon's own guard, run and breathing; mastery stances for the polearm and Black Leg.
Full Xbox pad support with prompts for the device in use.

versions.name: Masters of the Craft
versions.headline: Simpler skill points, a second guard for your weapon, new techniques, and new ways through the air.
versions.alt: The skills menu: a weapon's tree of glowing nodes in three branches on a night sky
added: One Combat pool and one Adventure pool; everything bought, gated by mastery; a lighter menu.
A second stance per weapon, toggled once owned, and drawn awakenings for five more weapons.
Two new techniques each for the polearm, hammer and twin axes; an air walk, a freefall tumble and new Acrobatics.

versions.name: Wanted
versions.headline: Rival crews who fight with your weapons and skills, an Admiralty that puts a price on your head, and a new opening.
versions.alt: The captain trading blows with a rival crew's mate in the snow at sunset
shots: rivals_crew
A rival crew waiting their turn at the side of a duel: one reading on a crate, one watching, their captain watching
wanted
A wanted poster on a village notice board: Wren Calloway, 64,000 gold
versions.clipAlt: The captain fights an Admiralty squad in grey coats on a snowy island
added: Captains run by the game with your weapons, moves, skills and ultimates, who read your spacing and punish whiffs.
Four crews with their own captains and lines: a meeting, duels in your style while the rest of the crew waits at the side at their own work, and a grudge either way.
Camera shots, letterboxed subtitles and voice blips; in co-op everyone presses skip.
Each captain's own, with wanted posters, townsfolk who know your face and shops that change their prices.
Grey ironclad patrols, bounty hunters ashore and three named officers with squads.
Lose to the Admiralty and break out of their brig to get your gear back.
A narrated storm at sea, then a fight on Captain Maren Holt's deck.
Strike with your own weapon while swimming; sharks and morays can be fought.
Spear, hammer, greatsword, twin-axe and black-leg pirates, each with its own moves.

versions.name: Beasts Reborn
versions.headline: The first piece of 1.20: every beast boss and roamer reworked, eight with new bodies, all with their own moves.
versions.alt: The captain trading blows with a rival crew's mate in the snow at sunset
added: Eight beasts rebuilt, two of them new two-legged giants, on a rig with jointed legs and slope-following bodies.
Every beast fights by its own list: readable wind-ups, openings after big moves, one knockdown each, no repeats.

versions.name: Polish
versions.headline: A pass over every island type: their own roofs and walls throughout, fuller villages, the Admiralty in grey.
versions.alt: The captain trading blows with a rival crew's mate in the snow at sunset
added: Camps, towers, gates and wells in each island type's own roofs and walls.

versions.name: The Fog Isle
versions.headline: A haunted fog isle: dead woods, the drowned and ghosts, lanterns to light, and the Drowned Captain on his wreck.
versions.alt: The captain trading blows with a rival crew's mate in the snow at sunset
added: Dead woods, a cursed fishing village, a graveyard and thick fog.
Drowned crews that get back up and shrug off bullets; ghosts that bullets pass through.
Light the old lanterns to thin the fog and keep the dead out of their glow.
A ghost captain who fights like you, on his wreck.

versions.name: Grounds and Wilds
versions.headline: Boss grounds of their own for every island type, and more along the ways between places.
versions.alt: The captain trading blows with a rival crew's mate in the snow at sunset
added: An ice grotto on the snow, a sunken ruin in the desert, a grove of standing stones in the forest.
Trunks, boulders, old walls, shrines, lone chests and left camps along the ways; more creatures and more people on the trails.

versions.name: The World
versions.headline: Every beast reworked with a ground of its own for every island type, a haunted fog isle under giant twisted trees, and more between places.
versions.alt: A pier at dusk leading into a fog-bound fishing village under giant twisted trees
shots: grotto
An ice grotto in a snowy mountainside: dark rock walls sheathed in blue ice round a frozen floor
sunken_ruin
A giant red scorpion in a sunken flagstone courtyard among broken desert walls
fog_ruins
Broken stone columns at dusk, giant twisted trees fading into the fog behind
added: Eight rebuilt bodies on a rig with jointed legs; every beast with its own moves, readable wind-ups and openings.
An ice grotto, a half-buried ruin and a ring of standing stones; the jungle keeps its canopy.
A fifth island type: giant twisted woods, the drowned and ghosts, lanterns that push back the fog, the Drowned Captain.
Trunks, boulders, old walls, shrines, lone chests, left camps, more creatures and people.
Each island type's own roofs and walls throughout, fuller villages.
Driftfruits, Will, the Leviathan, the lodestone and the Admiralty, everywhere you see them.

versions.name: The Canal City
versions.headline: The next pieces of 1.21: the canal city, the caravel and harbour vendors on the chain.
versions.alt: The royal capital's harbour and rooftops climbing to the palace (an early look, v1.18.1)
added: A lagoon city of shipbuilders: canals, bridges, water taxis, shops and quests.
A second ship to buy and sail; the sloop laid up with her upgrades.
Ship services by the pier at about half the chain's ports.

versions.name: The Arena
versions.headline: The third piece of 1.21: the capital's Grand Arena and its one-on-one ladder.
versions.alt: The royal capital's harbour and rooftops climbing to the palace (an early look, v1.18.1)
added: Onto the sand under a full crowd; six fighters on the ladder, a purse for every win.
The title and the Champion's Sabre, and a challenger a day to defend it against.

versions.name: The Palace
versions.headline: The second piece of 1.21: the palace open, its court and throne hall, and the Crown's errands.
versions.alt: The royal capital's harbour and rooftops climbing to the palace (an early look, v1.18.1)
added: The grounds, the road up, a court between the wings and a throne hall you walk into.
Three quests for the Lord Chamberlain, ending in an audience with Queen Ilsabet.

versions.name: The Docks and the Terrace
versions.headline: The first piece of 1.21: the capital's docks with its own shipwright, and the noble quarter's terrace.
versions.alt: The royal capital's harbour and rooftops climbing to the palace (an early look, v1.18.1)
added: A warehouse row to the wharf, Coyle's Yard (every refit, far from Brinehollow), a chandler and a fence.
A garden terrace under the palace wall and an outfitter to the court.

versions.name: Cities
versions.headline: The First Sea's first real cities: the royal capital and the canal city.
versions.alt: The royal capital's harbour and rooftops climbing to the palace (an early look, v1.18.1)
plan: The royal capital
A grand port with a palace on the heights, big markets and streets full of people.
The canal city
A city on the water, crossed by canals and bridges, with a shipyard.

versions.name: Combat and Gear
versions.headline: Every weapon polished, new weapon kinds, and armour and clothes with stats.
versions.alt: A twin-dagger combo in a jungle clearing (current build)
plan: A weapon pass
Animation and skill polish for every weapon, and a redesigned drawn-effects pass.
New weapons
Polearms, dual axes, a hammer and more.
New armour and clothes
With a stat system for armour and clothing.

versions.name: Strongholds and Driftfruits
versions.headline: Raids on Admiralty strongholds and pirate hideouts, and Driftfruits back, done right.
versions.alt: A trading post's palisade gate and watchtower (current build)
plan: Strongholds
Admiralty strongholds and pirate hideouts as raids.
Driftfruits return
Each fruit with its own moves, effects and tree, real trade-offs, and co-op rescues from the sea.
Fruit-user enemies
Enemies who wield fruits, from one world pool: a fruit is free again when its user falls.

versions.name: The Road to 2.0
versions.headline: More of the sea, more to fight, ships to work toward, and the Admiralty on your trail.
versions.alt: A Leviathan rearing over the sloop in a storm (current build)
plan: The sea between
The Kraken at shipwrecks, sea monsters, merchant and treasure ships, storms and whirlpools with purpose.
Enemies
More mob variations for every island type.
Ships to work toward
A fast caravel, a brig, a galleon and an oddball submarine, bought at the canal city's shipyard, each with its own upgrades.
Hunted
Admiralty patrols and pursuit, and named Admiralty captains tracking you down the chain.
Gear to make your own
Upgrading, effects and renaming for blue gear and up, and more clothing and looks.

versions.name: The First Sea
versions.headline: The first official release: a complete First Sea chain, from Brinehollow to a big final boss.
versions.alt: The sloop at sunset (current build)
plan: A complete First Sea
Every island type, the cities and the sea between them.
The finale
The first big, heavy boss fight at the end of the First Sea chain.
